audience.programmeDescription: This English-taught degree applies engineering to questions in health and medicine, including imaging, devices and biomaterials.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Groningen example uses the Biomaterials Science and Engineering minor. The UCR options emphasize biomedical science and technology, health technology design, or biomedical data and image analysis.

cellNotes.text: Groningen models transport in biological systems. UCR studies circulation and other body systems in Human Physiology.
Both study cell structure, signaling and division.
Both relate human anatomical structure to function. Groningen also includes physiology in this course.
Both study biomolecules and biochemical processes, including proteins and metabolism.
Both examine immune recognition and responses. UCR focuses on infection and host defenses.
Both use numerical methods for computational problems. UCR teaches Python separately.
Both use differentiation and integration for quantitative problems. UCR combines calculus with other mathematical methods.
Both use vectors, matrices and linear transformations.
Groningen studies the physics of medical imaging systems. UCR studies how to process images.
Both analyze signal and system behavior using transforms and frequency response.
Both develop probability and statistical inference for interpreting data.
Both develop image processing and analysis. UCR teaches general methods such as filtering and segmentation.
Groningen develops computation within the advanced biomedical engineering sequence.
Both develop concepts, specifications and prototypes. UCR works on general consumer products.
Groningen prepares students for biomedical engineering research. UCR offers general methods and statistics.
Groningen studies philosophy of science and research integrity. UCR studies broader ethical theories.
Groningen applies mechanics to biological structures and movement.
Groningen studies material properties for engineering applications.
Groningen develops experimental physics skills in the laboratory.
Groningen studies how materials interact with biological systems.
Both develop microbiology through bacterial work. The UCR lab also uses protein and DNA techniques.
Groningen credits safe microbiological techniques alongside its microbiology course.
Groningen studies the dynamics and vibration of mechanical systems.
Groningen teaches mathematical tools for biomedical engineering problems.
Groningen applies design methods to biomedical products. UCR offers general product design.
Groningen develops electricity and magnetism for engineering.
Groningen applies ethical reasoning to biomedical engineering.
Groningen teaches thermodynamics as a dedicated engineering subject.
Groningen studies waves and optics as a dedicated engineering subject.
Groningen offers a dedicated electronics course.
Groningen applies specialist biomaterials methods in the laboratory.
Groningen studies fabrication for biomedical applications.
Groningen develops biomedical measurement and instrumentation.
Groningen studies polymers for biomedical applications.
Groningen studies how to characterize material surfaces.
Groningen develops ethical reasoning for the research project.
Groningen studies tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.
Groningen requires a supervised 15 EC research or design project. UCR shows optional independent research separately.

notes.text: Groningen combines engineering design with mechanics, electronics, materials science, specialist laboratories and a required project. The UCR options combine related biomedical study with data analysis, robotics, product design and innovation.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENBUSI311.name: Transnational Business Law
BENBUSI311.text: Transnational Business Law studies legal frameworks for cross-border business, including contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Comparative and international perspectives support analysis of legal risks through discussions, problem-based assignments and an arbitration simulation.

source.reviewNote: Compared with the current selected workbook field. Retained the existing description as a faithful account; updated its source provenance.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

source.reviewNote: CP089: reviewed the unchanged official description against current course content. The existing text supports the stated scope.

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.text: Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.

source.reviewNote: Compared with the current selected workbook field. Revised the description to retain supported academic scope and activities without superseded or unsupported details.

BENENTR312.name: International Business & Governance
BENENTR312.text: Examines how trade, globalisation and political, cultural and technological conditions shape international business decisions. Students analyse governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate a business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.text: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.text: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.

DISARIN311.text: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.text: Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.

Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. Medical images, anatomical drawing, human-specimen material and guided practicals develop spatial reasoning, including observation in a dissection room. HCBBIOM312.name: Infection & Immunity
HCBBIOM312.text: Explores fundamental processes in immunology such as recognition of self vs non‑self, lymphocyte receptor development and innate and adaptive immune responses. Examines host‑pathogen interactions, inflammation, tissue damage and immunopathology.

HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease
HCBBIOM313.text: Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease. Students connect anatomy and physiology with symptoms, disease mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis across digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine and nervous systems. Clinical cases and an imaginary-disease assignment develop coherent pathophysiological explanations.

HCBCOGN112.text: Neurobiology studies nervous systems and behaviour through comparative anatomy, evolution and physiology. Students examine animal behaviour, research models, welfare and research ethics, then connect biological rhythms and regulatory behaviour to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. Comparative-anatomy work and a literature-based report apply neurobiological concepts.
